correctness.rationale: For p>M, the exact excess is D=(M(M+1)-(p-M)(q-M))/2. Under abundance D<pq, so a divisor subset representing D cannot use a divisor containing both odd primes. The remaining three binary divisor blocks realize exactly x+py+qz with 0<=x,y,z<=M, proving the criterion. Abundance also gives finite p,q bounds. Exhaustive exact-integer checks for a<=4 agree with direct divisor subset-sum in every bounded candidate.

originality.rationale: The foundational 2013 paper gives general excess and np criteria, and the 2020 paper classifies the two-distinct-prime family and treats higher layered cases. Searches of those sources, later Zumkeller work, OEIS, synonymous formulations, low-exponent slices, and the SCOPE archive did not locate the explicit 2^a p q reduction or the complete a<=4 exception lists. Originality remains to the best of our knowledge with residual risk from differently notated specializations.

value.rationale: The theorem converts an infinite three-prime divisor-partition family into an automatic infinite region plus a rigorously finite exceptional computation for every fixed binary exponent. It also completely classifies the first four exponents and identifies explicit abundant non-Zumkeller exceptions.
